subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): bound auth-profile JSON reads with size cap

question: Should OpenClaw permanently reject auth-profile JSON stores above 10 MiB by treating them as unavailable credentials under the existing recovery guidance?
rationale: The code safely enforces the chosen limit, but the numeric cap and the user-facing consequence for a valid oversized credential store are product and compatibility policy rather than a mechanical correctness choice.

options.title: Accept the 10 MiB policy
options.body: Confirm that oversized auth stores should be skipped with the existing no-credential guidance, then refresh the branch against current main before merge.

options.title: Add explicit oversized-store recovery
options.body: Require a targeted diagnostic or Doctor remediation path so users can distinguish an oversized valid store from a missing credential source before merging.

options.title: Pause the cap change
options.body: Do not add a hard limit until maintainers choose a different size policy or recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the 10 MiB policy
recommendation.body: Confirm that oversized auth stores should be skipped with the existing no-credential guidance, then refresh the branch against current main before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this contributor to the concrete implementation, although a current-main feature owner should make the policy decision.
